title: What a Name Means: Namespaces, Private Names and Remapping

questions.question: Two robots each run a lidar driver that publishes scan. What puts them on different topics?
options: Each node's name is resolved against its own namespace: /robot1/scan and /robot2/scan, apart, while an absolute /scan would be the same for both
Each driver adds a random suffix to its topics when it starts, so /scan_a1 and /scan_b7 are apart
The bus keeps a separate set of topics for every machine on the network
The two drivers are built with different topic names for each robot
questions.explanation: The node writes scan, and the bus name is the namespace plus that. Give each robot its own namespace and one program serves both.

questions.question: For node lidar_driver in /robot1, what does ~/status mean?
options: /robot1/status: a private name is put in the node's namespace
/robot1/lidar_driver/status: a private name goes inside a namespace named for the node
/lidar_driver/status: a private name ignores the namespace
/status: the tilde stands for the root
questions.explanation: The tilde is the node's own corner: its namespace and then its name. Status and parameters belong there.

questions.question: Which of these is not a valid topic name?
options: a//b, which has an empty part, and so do names with a trailing slash, a space, or a part starting with a digit
/a/b, because an absolute name may not have two parts
~/status, because a tilde is not a letter, digit or underscore
_hidden, because a name may not start with an underscore
questions.explanation: The rules allow letters, digits, underscores and slashes, with no empty part, no leading digit in a part, and a tilde only at the very start.

questions.question: What is wrong with a node that publishes to /scan?
options: Nothing: an absolute name is the safest, since it cannot be changed by a namespace
It is private, so no other node can subscribe to it
The name is absolute and ignores the namespace, so two robots share one topic with two publishers
It cannot be remapped from outside
questions.explanation: A leading slash means the name is taken as written. Run on two robots, both publish to the same topic and their scans are mixed.

questions.question: What does a remap rule apply to?
options: The name as written in the node, before the namespace is added
Every topic whose last part matches, in any namespace
Only private names, since those are the node's own
The resolved name: the same rule in a node in /robot2 is about /robot2/scan and does not apply to /robot1/scan
questions.explanation: The rule is resolved in the node's namespace like any other name, and compared with the resolved topic. So a node in /robot2 does not touch /robot1's topics.

questions.question: What does the root namespace contribute to a name?
options: One slash, so scan in the root is //scan
Nothing, so scan in the root is /scan and not //scan
The node's name, so scan in the root is /lidar_driver/scan
An error: a node must be given a namespace
questions.explanation: robot1/, /robot1 and /robot1/ are one namespace, and the empty one is the root. The root adds nothing in front of the name.
